question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{18}∼N(2,{6}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $18$ from a normal population, calculate $P(|\overset{―}{X}|<1.05).$ *Hint: Value tables of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2578\,$ $\,0.2546\,$ $\,0.2514\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.2912\,$ $\,0.2877\,$ $\,0.2843\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3264\,$ $\,0.3228\,$ $\,0.3192\,$

$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-2.2\,$ $\,0.0119\,$ $\,0.0116\,$ $\,0.0113\,$
$\,-2.1\,$ $\,0.0154\,$ $\,0.0150\,$ $\,0.0146\,$
$\,-2.0\,$ $\,0.0197\,$ $\,0.0192\,$ $\,0.0188\,$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(2,\frac{{6}^{2}}{18}) \\  & ∼N(2,2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|<1.05).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|<1.05) & =P(-1.05<\overset{―}{X}<1.05) \\  & =P(\frac{-1.05-2}{\sqrt{2}}<Z<\frac{1.05-2}{\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =P(-2.16<Z<-0.67) \\  & =Φ(-0.67)-Φ(-2.16)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.67) & =0.2514, \\ Φ(-2.16) & =0.0154.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|<1.05) & =Φ(-0.67)-Φ(-2.16) \\  & =0.2514-0.0154 \\  & =0.2360.\end{aligned}
$$
